reviewer: Claude (agent). Judged from contact sheets, seam strips, frame snapshots and measured QA. The film was not auditioned by ear and not watched end-to-end at real speed.

criteria.question: One clear focal point per beat; reading order is obvious.
criteria.notes: One idea per zone: the colour strip (s1), the jelly and zone label (s2), the counter (s3), the dot field and 76% (s4). The 100-dot pictogram is the strongest image in the film. s2 is the weakest hierarchy: a small jelly and one label in a lot of water.

criteria.question: Type roles are consistent; sizes respect the floor; no orphans or awkward breaks.
criteria.notes: Oswald uppercase with wide tracking for labels and Inter/Plex Mono for support; all above the size floor (no text-size-floor finding). The mono labels are small and dim by design (24 px, low contrast ink on dark); they carry secondary information only.

criteria.question: Layouts are intentional in every format (not stretched or cropped landscape).
criteria.notes: Landscape only. Off-centre subjects and deep negative space as the profile prescribes, but the tool flags four scenes at 17-26% content coverage; I accepted this as the idiom and did not waive it, so it stays visible as an open lead.

criteria.question: Holds match reading time; rhythm varies; nothing drags or rushes.
criteria.notes: Slow by design (7-13 s beats). s4's opening was an empty near-black stretch of ~8 s; it now has the sweeping 1,000 m line and foreshadowing sparks. s3's first half (the '1' with slowly closing lines) is still quiet.

criteria.question: All text is legible at delivery size with sufficient contrast.
criteria.notes: Contrast by eye is good on the numerals and the closing line; the small mono captions and the 76% source line are low in contrast and size and would be hard on a phone in daylight. Not measured on image backgrounds (the tool declines to guess).

criteria.question: Palette and texture follow the chosen style system and direction.
criteria.notes: Teal to black, one amber accent and one bioluminescent green; reads as cinematic-dark. The plates are procedural gradients with particles and caustics, so they read as stylised water, not photographed water: that is stated in the brief and report, not hidden.

criteria.question: Each transition carries meaning or continuity; none are decorative filler.
criteria.notes: Vertical push (the camera continues downward), a slow dissolve into the pressure abstraction, an iris onto the dark, and a dissolve into the close. The iris shows a black disc growing over the amber '1,090' for ~0.3 s, which reads as a porthole closing on the dark but is the least elegant seam.

criteria.question: Motion vocabulary is consistent across scenes.
criteria.notes: Consistent vocabulary: a persistent depth gauge, slow parallax, light that is subtracted then re-added as animal-made light. The gauge sits out the surface-pressure baseline and returns counting the same descent as the atmospheres, which fixed an earlier contradiction.

criteria.question: No repetitive looping filler or motion without purpose.
criteria.notes: Particles, caustics and jelly pulses are continuous but each belongs to the water column. The grain and vignette are static overlays.

criteria.question: No unintended static stretches; intentional holds are marked.
criteria.notes: No objective failures; slow drifts are reported as 'slow-drift' notes, not holds. Two stretches were low-energy before fixing (s4 opening, the end), now covered by a luminous line and sparks; the end hold is declared minimal and reported as a waiver.

criteria.question: No accidental overlaps, clipping or safe-area violations.
criteria.notes: Text-collision and clipping checks clean on the final composition. Earlier defects found and fixed: depth needle over numerals, counter against the gauge, labels overlapping the dot grid, closing line through the dots, dots clipped by the frame edge.

criteria.question: Clear opening, progression and ending; the last frame holds long enough.
criteria.notes: Descent in four steps then a one-line landing; the 76% payoff is a picture and its scope (17 years of video off California) is on screen. The film ends smaller and quieter than it began.

verdict: An agent's critique, not user acceptance. Sound design (a bed per zone, 76 synchronised bells) was verified only by measurement: loudness -17.8 LUFS (inside the +/-2 LU tolerance, at its edge), no clipping gate failures.
pass_rule: Every criterion scored 1-5 with evidence (frame or contact-sheet paths); all >= 3 and mean >= 3.5.
